function.name: generate_image_tool

The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below are two ways you can launch a **Compute Engine** VM that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# Replace <PROJECT_ID> and <ZONE> with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-demo \
    --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
    --zone=${ZONE} \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU / 30 GB RAM – adjust if needed
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: install GPU drivers
```

### Optional: Install NVIDIA drivers automatically

Create a small shell script called `startup.sh` in the same directory:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential dkms
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-ubuntu2004.pin
sudo mv cuda-ubuntu2004.pin /etc/apt/preferences.d/cuda-repository-pin-600
wget http://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/12.2.0/local_installers/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-535.54.03-1_amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-535.54.03-1_amd64.deb
sudo cp /var/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local/cuda-*-keyring.gpg /usr/share/keyrings/
sudo apt-key add /var/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local/cuda-*-keyring.gpg
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y cuda-drivers
```

Make sure the script is executable:

```bash
chmod +x startup.sh
```

When the instance boots, the script will run and install the latest NVIDIA driver that supports the RTX A6000.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to use the raw REST endpoint, here’s a minimal JSON body you can POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      },
      "autoDelete": true,
      "type": "PERSISTENT"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y build-essential dkms\nwget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-ubuntu2004.pin\nsudo mv cuda-ubuntu2004.pin /etc/apt/preferences.d/cuda-repository-pin-600\nwget http://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/12.2.0/local_installers/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-535.54.03-1_amd64.deb\nsudo dpkg -i cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-535.54.03-1_amd64.deb\nsudo cp /var/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local/cuda-*-keyring.gpg /usr/share/keyrings/\nsudo apt-key add /var/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local/cuda-*-keyring.gpg\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y cuda-drivers"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Send it via a POST request to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/us-central1-a/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json
```

Replace `<PROJECT_ID>` with your actual project ID and supply a valid OAuth 2.0 bearer token that has the `compute.instances.create` scope.

---

### Quick sanity check

After creation, verify the GPU is visible:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-demo --command "nvidia-smi"
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed along with its driver version.

Happy computing!
